description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 60% to 85%. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, starts at approximately 64% accuracy and increases to around 71% as the co-occurrence number grows. The MEND method, shown with brown diamonds and a solid line, begins at about 70.5% and rises to approximately 80% at the highest co-occurrence number. The FT method, depicted with blue triangles and a solid line, starts at around 65% and increases to about 73%. The MEMIT method, represented by purple squares and a solid line, begins at roughly 69.5% and increases to about 77%. The ROME method, shown with green squares and a solid line, starts at approximately 74% and increases to about 82%. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME achieving the highest accuracy across the range.
